lessons.title: Lesson 1: Hello World & Main Method
lessons.html:
Your First Java Program

Java is a class-based, object-oriented language especially designed for web development.

Basic Structure:

  • public class - Main class declaration
  • public static void main - Entry point where program starts
  • System.out.println - Prints text to console
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Java!");
    }
}

Compile: javac HelloWorld.java
Run: java HelloWorld
Practice: Change message to your name!

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Variables & Data Types
lessons.html:
Variables and Data Types

All variables must be declared with their type before use. Java is statically typed.

Primitive Types:

TypeSizeExample
int4 bytes42
double8 bytes3.14
boolean1 bittrue
char2 bytes'A'
public class Variables {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int age = 25;
        double salary = 50000.50;
        String name = "Alice";
        boolean isActive = true;
        System.out.println(name + " is " + age + " years old");
    }
}

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Control Structures
lessons.html:
Control Flow Statements

Control structures change the order of execution based on conditions.

if/else:

int age = 20;
if (age >= 18) {
    System.out.println("Adult");
} else {
    System.out.println("Minor");
}

switch:

int day = 1;
switch(day) {
    case 1: System.out.println("Monday"); break;
    case 2: System.out.println("Tuesday"); break;
    default: System.out.println("Other day");
}

Loops:

for(int i=0; i<5; i++) {
    System.out.print(i + " ");
}
// Output: 0 1 2 3 4

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Methods & Arrays
lessons.html:
Methods and Arrays

Methods are reusable blocks of code. Arrays store multiple values of same type.

Method Example:

public static int add(int a, int b) {
    return a + b;
}

Arrays:

public class ArraysExample {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5};
        for(int num : numbers) {
            System.out.println(num);
        }
        System.out.println("Length: " + numbers.length);
    }
}

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Object-Oriented Basics
lessons.html:
Classes and Objects

Java is object-oriented. Everything revolves around classes and objects.

Class Definition:

class Person {
    String name;
    int age;
    
    void introduce() {
        System.out.println("Hi, I'm " + name);
    }
}

Creating Objects:

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Person p = new Person();
        p.name = "Bob";
        p.age = 30;
        p.introduce();  // Hi, I'm Bob
    }
}
